title: Isandro and the Inheritance
premise: Oscar Vasquez, a night-shift dispatcher for Marisol Cabs, has built a reputation on closing every case that crosses their radio — lost drivers, missing fares, debts of honor. When a drowned stranger washes up at Pier 9 wearing clothes lifted from Oscar's own closet, the police make Oscar both witness and suspect, and the only clue is a taxi ledger written in a cipher their late mentor used for fares that never appeared on any books. As Oscar decodes the ledger with help from their found family — a retired driver, a teenage hacker who answers the night line, and Isandro Reyes, the detective assigned to the case whom Oscar is rapidly falling for — they uncover a smuggling ring that has been running through the cab company for thirty years, protected by the very people who raised them. The tide eventually gives up what it took: a second body and the ledger's final page naming the killer, forcing Oscar to choose between loyalty to their chosen family and the truth Isandro deserves. In the end Oscar turns over the evidence, the ring falls, and they and Isandro begin something honest on the morning shift.
about_author: Coral Oyelaran is a former harbor-city journalist who spent three years riding night shifts with taxi dispatchers before writing fiction. She lives near the water and writes mysteries about the people who keep cities running while everyone else sleeps.

chapters.title: The Night Line
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A routine shift establishes Oscar's pride in closing every case and introduces the dispatch crew: Ruthie the retired driver, Dev the teenage night-line volunteer. Emotional beat: comfort in routine, faint unease when a fare request comes from a number that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Clothes That Fit Too Well
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Called to Pier 9 after a driver reports a body, Oscar recognizes their own jacket and shirt on the drowned man. Police arrive; Detective Isandro Reyes takes Oscar's statement with unsettling gentleness. Beat: shock curdling into the fear of being seen.

chapters.title: Person of Interest
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He reviews the scene: no wallet, clothes tailored to someone else's measurements, saltwater in lungs but bruises predating drowning. He suspects Oscar knows more than they admit. Beat: professional curiosity sharpening into personal fascination.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Searching the dispatch office for anything connecting them to the victim, Oscar finds their late mentor Sal's old fare ledgers — columns of numbers that repeat too neatly. Beat: grief reopening as suspicion.

chapters.title: Sal's Cipher
chapters.summary: Oscar and Dev's POV alternating. Dev recognizes the repeating numbers as a book cipher keyed to the company's route map. The first decoded entry names Pier 9 and a date thirty years back. Beat: thrill of discovery shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Questions at Dawn
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro interviews Ruthie, who stonewalls with practiced warmth. He notices the cab company's records have gaps exactly where the ledger's entries fall. Beat: frustration, and the first crack in his certainty about Oscar.

chapters.title: The Fare That Never Was
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Decoded entries reveal decades of 'ghost fares' — pickups logged but never completed, all ending at the piers. Oscar realizes Sal was logging smuggled cargo, or people. Beat: betrayal of a dead man's memory.

chapters.title: Coffee, Interrogation Style
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isandro buys Oscar coffee off the record; they trade half-truths and find themselves enjoying it. Both withhold the ledger. Beat: reluctant attraction, guilt humming underneath.

chapters.title: Ruthie Knows Something
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar confronts Ruthie gently; she warns them to stop pulling threads, mentioning 'the partners' before catching herself. Beat: the first fracture in found-family trust.

chapters.title: Second Body, Rising Tide
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The tide delivers a second corpse near Pier 12 — the missing taxi driver from chapter one's ghost log. Now it's murder, and the ledger becomes evidence Oscar is illegally withholding. Beat: stakes escalate; Isandro's dilemma begins.

chapters.title: Dev Hacks the Archive
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev pulls digitized police files and finds a thirty-year-old case: a dockworker's disappearance, closed as accidental drowning, Sal listed as a witness. Beat: the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Someone follows Oscar home from the depot — a gray sedan with government plates that aren't government. Oscar loses it in the container yards. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Partners
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV (first time). Flashback-tinged chapter: Ruthie remembers the original four 'partners' who built Marisol Cabs — Sal, herself, and two men now respectable. One of them is the victim's uncle. Beat: loyalty as a cage.

chapters.title: Off the Books
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. His captain orders him to narrow the suspect pool to Oscar. Isandro resents being handled and starts his own quiet inquiry into the department's old Pier 9 file. Beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: The Cipher Deepens
chapters.summary: Oscar and Dev's POV. The ledger's later pages use a second key — Sal's personal route codes. Decoded fragments reference 'the passenger' repeatedly, singular, precious, recurring monthly for years. Beat: mystery deepening from cargo to person.

chapters.title: A Date with a Suspect
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isandro asks Oscar to dinner 'to go over timelines.' It is transparently not about timelines. They almost tell each other the truth twice and don't. Beat: love against duty, first real ache.

chapters.title: Broken Window at the Depot
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The dispatch office is ransacked; the ledgers are gone — except Oscar took the key volume home days earlier. Whoever searched knew what to look for. Beat: violation, and relief that becomes its own burden.

chapters.title: The Uncle
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro interviews Emilio Vasquez — no relation to Oscar — a port authority board member and one of the original partners. The man is silk and menace. Beat: the shape of the enemy emerges.

chapters.title: What Ruthie Buried
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Ruthie tells Oscar part of the truth: the ghost fares moved people fleeing danger, off-grid, protected by Sal. But twelve years ago the operation changed hands and changed nature. Beat: sympathy complicating loyalty.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Cross-referencing dates, Oscar realizes 'the passenger' was a single person moved monthly for a decade — someone hidden, sheltered, perhaps imprisoned by protection. Beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Wire
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro wires Oscar for a recorded conversation with Emilio without telling his captain. Oscar agrees, terrified, trusting Isandro more than the badge. Beat: intimacy forged in risk.

chapters.title: Dinner with Emilio
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The recorded dinner: Emilio offers Oscar money and silence, lets slip that Sal 'drowned doing the right thing,' then threatens Dev. Oscar walks out shaking, having gotten enough. Beat: courage costing something.

chapters.title: The Recording Vanishes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The wire recording is wiped from evidence systems — someone inside the department. Isandro realizes he can't trust his own house. Beat: isolation; the case turns inward.

chapters.title: Dev Disappears
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Dev misses the night line; their apartment shows signs of a hurried exit, staged or real. A text arrives from Dev's phone: 'stop digging.' Beat: fear for found family eclipsing everything.

chapters.title: The Gray Sedan Again
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Oscar and Isandro, now fully allies off the record, trace the sedan to a private security firm owned jointly by Emilio and the fourth partner, Marcus Hale — a beloved city councilman. Beat: the conspiracy's true breadth revealed.

chapters.title: Sal's Last Route
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following Sal's final coded route, Oscar finds a boathouse key taped under an old bench at Pier 14. Inside: Sal's real journal, and photographs of the passenger — a young woman, alive, dated last month. Beat: hope igniting inside grief.

chapters.title: The Journal
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Reading Sal's journal aloud to Oscar and Ruthie, Dev (returned, having hid from the firm) learns the whole history: the woman is the daughter of the drowned dockworker, hidden from Emilio since childhood. Beat: the mystery's heart laid bare.

chapters.title: Where Is She Now
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The latest ledger entry points to a decommissioned ferry terminal. Oscar wants to go tonight; Isandro insists on procedure; they clash hard. Beat: love against duty at full pressure.

chapters.title: Hale's Gala
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At Councilman Hale's waterfront fundraiser, Oscar and Isandro split up — Oscar lifts access to Hale's private marina schedule while Isandro provokes Emilio into a partial confession caught on Dev's rig. Beat: elegant tension, near-catastrophe.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Blue
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. His captain suspends him, tipped by an anonymous complaint quoting the dinner wire verbatim. There is a leak, and it sits above the captain. Beat: the system itself revealed as compromised.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Weather report: a storm surge will flood the ferry terminal's lower levels within two days. Whatever happens to the passenger must happen before the tide gives up or destroys what it holds. Beat: clock started.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Choice
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Ruthie confesses she has been feeding the partners information about Oscar's investigation — under threat to Dev. She offers to walk into Emilio's office wearing a wire instead. Beat: loyalty finally choosing truth.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The team preps: Dev on comms, Ruthie making the approach, Oscar and Isandro set to breach the terminal when Emilio's men move the woman. Beat: found family arming itself with purpose.

chapters.title: The Ferry Terminal
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The raid goes sideways; Ruthie's wire is discovered, gunfire in the dark, and Oscar finds the hidden apartment behind the terminal wall — empty, warm, recently lived in. Beat: despair at the edge of triumph.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Up
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The storm surge dislodges a submerged car at Pier 9 containing Sal's remains and Emilio's thirty-year-old murder weapon. Physical evidence, finally undeniable. Beat: the sea settling its accounts.

chapters.title: Emilio's Endgame
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cornered, Emilio takes the passenger — Elena — to a boat to flee. Dev's intercepted radio traffic gives Oscar the dock. Beat: all threads converging at speed.

chapters.title: Pier 9, High Water
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax: Oscar confronts Emilio on the storm-lashed pier, talks him off the boat long enough for Isandro and coast guard units to close the net. Oscar nearly goes into the water saving Elena. Beat: every theme colliding; love and truth win together.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Arrests cascade — Emilio, the captain, complicit officers. Hale resigns rather than face charges. Isandro formally clears Oscar, then asks them to dinner with no pretense at all. Beat: exhale; tenderness earned.

chapters.title: Closing Out the Book
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar closes Sal's ledger for good, writes one honest final entry, and pins Sal's route map above the dispatch desk. Ruthie retires into daylight hours; Dev gets a scholarship funded quietly by Ruthie's testimony deal. Beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: First Light Shift
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Weeks later: sunrise over the harbor, Oscar and Isandro sharing coffee on the pier where it began, Elena rebuilding her life nearby. The night line rings; Oscar answers, smiling. Beat: peace, continuity, love chosen over fear.
